Load All Datasets
------------------------
```{r}
data_files = list.files(
  path = "../Input/",        # directory to search within
  pattern = "*RData$", # regex pattern, some explanation below
  recursive = F,          # search subdirectories
  full.names = TRUE          # return the full path
)



lapply(data_files,load,.GlobalEnv)

```

Harmonize Outcomes  by Study
----------------------
```{r}
AIRWEIGHS_Outcomes <- AIRWEIGHS_data_list[["AIRWEIGHS_Epi"]] %>% 
  dplyr::select(Child_PID = PID,Visit = aw_visit) %>%
  mutate(Asthma = 1) 
```


```{r}
CCREOH_Outcomes <- CCREOH_data_list[["CCREOH_Epi"]] %>% 
  dplyr::select(Mat_PID = PID,Child_PID = CHILD_PID,Birthweight = b031,Low_Birthweight = b031a,
                Gest_Age_Birth = b034b,Preterm_Birth = b034c,APGAR_5 = b035b,Low_APGAR = b035d,
                Social_Composite = socialemotional_composite,Languge_Composite = language_composite,
                Motor_Composite = motor_composite,BMI = v111c,Perc_Stress = v140n1,Depression = v150n2,
                Cognitive_Composite = cognitive_composite) %>%
  # LOW_BIRTHWEIGHT POLARITY (2026-08-10): raw b031a is coded 1 = low (n=66),
  # 2 = not low (n=583), while PARENTs -- the only other Low_Birthweight cohort --
  # uses 1 = low / 0 = not low. standardize_binary_outcome() in
  # Targeted_ExWAS_Replication.Rmd passes {0,1} through unchanged but otherwise
  # maps the HIGHER SORTED level to the case, so CCREOH's "2 = not low" was being
  # modelled as the case and its sign came out inverted relative to PARENTs.
  # Recoded to the project's 1 = case / 0 = control convention.
  mutate(Low_Birthweight = dplyr::case_when(Low_Birthweight == 1 ~ 1,
                                            Low_Birthweight == 2 ~ 0,
                                            TRUE ~ NA_real_))

```

```{r}
ELEMENT_Outcomes <- ELEMENT_data_list[["ELEMENT_Epi"]] %>%
  dplyr::select(Child_PID = PID_child,Mat_PID = PID_mother,Gest_Age_Birth = DELIVERY_GESTAGE,
                Birthweight = DELIVERY_WEIGHT,APGAR_1 = DELIVERY_APGAR1MIN, APGAR_5 = DELIVERY_APGAR5MIN) %>%
  # BIRTHWEIGHT UNITS (2026-08-10): DELIVERY_WEIGHT is a CHARACTER column holding
  # whole kilograms ("1","2","3","4") plus "." for missing. It is genuinely a
  # weight, not a category code -- HHEAR's own ELEMENT_Harmonized object calls the
  # same data "Child-Human-Weight-Kilogram-Birth". Converted to GRAMS so it pools
  # with CCREOH/CEHC/MADRES/PARENTs (the ExWAS reports UNSTANDARDIZED betas, and
  # ExWAS_Location_Heterogeneity compares betas ACROSS studies, so a kg-vs-g mix
  # reads as effect heterogeneity).
  # CAVEAT: only 4 distinct values, i.e. 1000 g resolution -- a weak continuous
  # outcome. Kept per user decision 2026-08-10; revisit if it dominates a panel.
  # The explicit na_if(".") also stops this character column from coercing the
  # WHOLE pooled Birthweight column to character via rbindlist.
  mutate(Birthweight = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(dplyr::na_if(as.character(Birthweight), "."))) * 1000) %>%
  # DELIVERY_GESTAGE is likewise a character column using "." for missing (37
  # rows), which was coercing the WHOLE pooled Gest_Age_Birth column to
  # character across all cohorts. Values are already decimal weeks, so this is
  # a type fix only -- no rescaling.
  mutate(Gest_Age_Birth = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(dplyr::na_if(as.character(Gest_Age_Birth), "."))))
```

```{r}
SICAS_Outcomes <- SICAS_data_list[["SICAS_Epi"]] %>%
  # NOT A BIRTHWEIGHT (2026-08-10): raw `birth_weight` holds only the values
  # 1 (n=15) and 2 (n=149) -- 9.1% in level 1, and SICAS_Harmonized carries no
  # birth-weight column at all. That matches CCREOH's Low_Birthweight 1/2 coding
  # (66/583 = 10.2%), so this is a LOW-BIRTHWEIGHT INDICATOR that was misfiled
  # under Birthweight, where it entered the ExWAS as a binary "weight" outcome.
  # Remapped to Low_Birthweight with the project's 1 = case / 0 = control coding.
  dplyr::select(Child_PID = PID,Low_Birthweight = birth_weight,bmi,everything()) %>%
  mutate(Low_Birthweight = dplyr::case_when(Low_Birthweight == 1 ~ 1,
                                            Low_Birthweight == 2 ~ 0,
                                            TRUE ~ NA_real_)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-all_of(remove)) %>% 
  mutate(Asthma = 1)
```

```{r}
ZIP_Outcomes <- ZIP_data_list[["ZIP_EPI_1"]] %>% 
  dplyr::select(Child_PID = CHILD_PID,Mat_PID = MOTHER_PID,Preterm = deli_preterm1,
                Gest_Age_Birth = infant_weeks,APGAR_1 = infant_apgar_1min,APGAR_5 = infant_apgar_5min,infant_wt,infant_wt_unit) %>%
  # BIRTHWEIGHT UNITS BUG (fixed 2026-08-10). The old line was
  #   mutate(Birthweight = infant_wt/infant_wt_unit)
  # but `infant_wt_unit` is a UNIT CODE, not a divisor: it is 1 for n=893 and
  # 2 for n=2. Dividing by it silently HALVED the two unit-2 rows. Those two
  # carry infant_wt 7.0 and 8.8, i.e. POUNDS (code 2 = lb, code 1 = kg), so the
  # old expression returned 3.5/4.4 kg where the truth is 3.18/3.99 kg. It went
  # unnoticed because /2 happens to land in a plausible birthweight range.
  # Now an explicit per-code conversion, and the result is in GRAMS to match
  # CCREOH/CEHC/MADRES/PARENTs -- see the ELEMENT note on why units must agree.
  mutate(Birthweight = dplyr::case_when(
    infant_wt_unit == 1 ~ infant_wt * 1000,        # kg -> g
    infant_wt_unit == 2 ~ infant_wt * 453.59237,   # lb -> g
    TRUE                ~ NA_real_
  )) %>%
  dplyr::select(-infant_wt,-infant_wt_unit)
```

```{r}
library(janitor)

yn_to_int <- function(x) {
  x_chr <- str_to_lower(trimws(as.character(x)))
  case_when(
    x_chr %in% c("yes", "y", "true", "t", "1") ~ 1L,
    x_chr %in% c("no",  "n", "false","f", "0") ~ 0L,
    x_chr %in% c("", "na", "n/a", "null")      ~ NA_integer_,
    TRUE ~ NA_integer_
  )
}

is_yes_no_col <- function(x) {
  vals <- str_to_lower(trimws(as.character(x)))
  vals <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
  vals <- vals[vals != ""]
  vals <- vals[!vals %in% c("na","n/a","null")]
  length(vals) > 0 && all(vals %in% c("yes","no","y","n","true","false","t","f","0","1"))
}



names(OBSS_data_list[["OBSS_EPI"]])

OBSS_Outcomes <- OBSS_data_list[["OBSS_EPI"]] %>% 
    select(Mat_PID = PID,everything()) %>% 
    mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(.x, "NA"))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is_yes_no_col), yn_to_int)) %>% 
    #clean_names() %>%
  # mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(.x, "NA"))) %>%
  # mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(.x, ""))) %>% 
    {
      base <- names(.) %>% str_remove("_[12]$")
      pairs <- base[base %in% str_remove(names(.), "_[12]$")]
      pairs <- unique(pairs[str_detect(names(.), paste0("^", pairs, "_[12]$"), negate = FALSE)])
      # coalesce each *_1 and *_2 into a single column
      reduce(unique(str_remove(names(.)[str_detect(names(.), "_[12]$")], "_[12]$")),
             ~ mutate(.x,
                      !!.y := coalesce(.x[[paste0(.y, "_1")]], .x[[paste0(.y, "_2")]])),
             .init = .) %>%
        select(-matches("_[12]$"))
    } %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.character), readr::parse_number, .names = "{.col}")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-all_of(c("group","race" ,"sex","ethnicity","smoking","weight"))) 


```

```{r}
    Pre_Bronchodilator_FEV1        = pre_fev1_a,
    Pre_Bronchodilator_FVC         = pre_fvc_a,
    Pre_Bronchodilator_FEV1_FVC    = pre_fev1_fvc_a,
    Pre_Bronchodilator_FEF25_75    = pre_fef_a,
    Ever_Wheeze                    = as1_spiro,
    Wheeze_Past_12_Months          = as2_spiro,
    Asthma_Ever                    = as6_spiro
  )


```


New cohorts (2026-08-10): GRAPHS / ATLAA / SWSD
----------------------
All three are MATERNAL-ONLY on the exposure side: every row in
Harmonized_Targeted for these cohorts has a Mat_PID and NO Child_PID. The ExWAS
splits into a `child` panel keyed on Child_PID and a `mat` panel keyed on
Mat_PID, so outcomes MUST be keyed on Mat_PID -- minting child PIDs would put
these birth outcomes in a panel with no exposures to join and produce zero
tasks. The infant birth outcomes therefore sit on the maternal row.

IMHRD is deliberately absent: it ships only year x analyte summary statistics
with no participant identifiers, so it cannot carry an outcome.

```{r}
# GRAPHS -- Ghana, maternal urine PAH/VOC. The workbook's only participant-level
# sheet is Participant_Metadata (5 columns); there are NO birth outcomes to map,
# so maternal BMI is the single ExWAS-eligible outcome.
# NOTE: GRAPHS will contribute no ExWAS results, because none of its 10 PAH/VOC
# analytes is measured by any other cohort that has a maternal BMI outcome
# (CCREOH/NHBCS/NYUWHS/OBSS/THS), so no pair reaches the n_studies >= 2
# filter. Included for completeness and so it lands automatically if GRAPHS
# birth outcomes ever arrive -- its NAP1/NAP2/PYR1/FLUO2 ARE the top eligible
# exposures for maternal Birthweight and Gest_Age_Birth.
GRAPHS_Outcomes <- GRAPHS_data_list[["GRAPHS_Epi"]] %>%
  dplyr::select(Mat_PID = PID, BMI = Maternal_BMI) %>%
  mutate(Mat_PID = as.character(Mat_PID))
```

```{r}
# ATLAA -- Atlanta, maternal serum PFAS. Units read off the workbook's
# "Data dictionary" sheet, NOT inferred from magnitude.
#   birth_weight   : "birthweight", Unit = grams  (930-4320) -> used as-is
#   FirstPretalBMI : "BMI at first prenatal visit", kg/m2    (sic, typo is in source)
#   birthga        : "Gestational age in weeks.days (wks.days)"  <-- SEE BELOW
#
# GESTATIONAL AGE IS wks.days, NOT DECIMAL WEEKS. "39.6" means 39 weeks 6 days
# = 39.857 weeks, not 39.6 weeks. Verified: every fractional digit is 0-6, none
# is 7/8/9, and no value carries more than one decimal place. Existing cohorts
# store true decimal weeks (NHBCS 39.14, MADRES 39.29, IMBEDD 33.57), so loading
# this raw would compress the fractional part by 10/7 and be silently
# inconsistent with them.
ATLAA_Outcomes <- ATLAA_data_list[["ATLAA_Epi"]] %>%
  dplyr::select(Mat_PID = Subjectid, Birthweight = birth_weight,
                Gest_Age_Birth = birthga, BMI = FirstPretalBMI) %>%
  mutate(
    Mat_PID        = as.character(Mat_PID),
    Birthweight    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Birthweight)),   # already grams
    BMI            = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(BMI)),
    Gest_Age_Birth = {
      ga   <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Gest_Age_Birth))
      wks  <- floor(ga)
      days <- round((ga - wks) * 10)      # one decimal place, values 0-6
      wks + days / 7
    }
  )
```

```{r}
# SWSD -- Thailand, maternal urine neonicotinoids. Units read off the workbook's
# "Dictionary" sheet:
#   birthwt : "Birth weight", Unit = kg  (1.21-4.05) -> x1000 to grams
#   BMI_v1  : "BMI at first visit", kg/m2
#   GA_wks  : "Gestational age (weeks)", 29-41, complete
#   GA_day  : "Gestational age (days)", takes EXACTLY the values 0-6 (uniform),
#             so it is the remainder day within the week, not a total-days count.
#             => decimal weeks = GA_wks + GA_day/7.
# GA_day is NA for 2 of 296 subjects while GA_wks is present for both; those two
# are coalesced to the whole week rather than dropped (at most 6/7 of a week of
# resolution lost, versus losing the subjects entirely).
# The raw sheet is one row per subject x trimester; SWSD_Epi is already
# distinct(), but distinct() is repeated here so a future reader change cannot
# silently duplicate maternal rows.
SWSD_Outcomes <- SWSD_data_list[["SWSD_Epi"]] %>%
  dplyr::select(Mat_PID = subjectid, Birthweight = birthwt,
                BMI = BMI_v1, GA_wks, GA_day) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(
    Mat_PID        = as.character(Mat_PID),
    Birthweight    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Birthweight)) * 1000,  # kg -> g
    BMI            = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(BMI)),
    Gest_Age_Birth = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(GA_wks)) +
                     dplyr::coalesce(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(GA_day)), 0) / 7
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-GA_wks, -GA_day)
```

```{r}
rm(Outcomes_Data_All)
Pattern1<-grep("Outcomes",names(.GlobalEnv),value=TRUE)
bind_list<-do.call("list",mget(Pattern1))

Outcomes_Data_All <- rbindlist( bind_list, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE,idcol = "Study" )

# Participant IDs are CHARACTER across all harmonized artifacts (2026-08).
# Some cohorts (e.g. ATLAA) use alphanumeric IDs such as "E0604", which cannot be
# numeric, so Harmonized_Targeted / Harmonized_SDOH carry character IDs. Coerce
# here too so joins between Outcomes and those tables don't fail on type mismatch.
Outcomes_Data_All <- Outcomes_Data_All %>%
  mutate(across(any_of(c("Child_PID","Mat_PID")), as.character))

```


```{r}
names(Outcomes_Data_All)
save(Outcomes_Data_All,file = "../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Harmonized_Outcomes.RData")
write_csv(Outcomes_Data_All, file = "../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Harmonized_Outcomes.csv")
```
